title: Verify permission gating of Simple-Flow settings and work-order actions (UI gating is the v1 pass criterion)
section_path: Test Cases > Simple Flow > API — Permissions
refs: SV-8183 (§9.1 Bulk Receive gate / §9.2 accept enforcement)
preconds:
1. Signed in with API access.
  2. A relevant Simple-Flow setting (e.g. Require Vendor Invoice Number) is ON.
steps:
1. As a role that lacks the mapped permission, confirm the gated setting or action is hidden or unavailable in the app.
  2. As that same role, try the same setting change directly through the API (bypassing the app) and note the response.
  3. As a role that lacks the completion or review sign-off permission, try to complete a work order and to sign off a review directly through the API and note the responses.
  4. As a role that only has Work Orders: Create & Edit, try to receive parts onto a work order through the API and note the response.
  5. For each of the eleven roles in turn, call the Bulk Receive 'accept' action directly through the API (the 'Receive Selected' / Bulk Receive submit) and note the response for each role.
expected:
1. In the app, a role without the mapped permission does not see or cannot use the gated setting or action (this is the v1 pass criterion).
  2. The Work Order settings save is also blocked at the backend: the unauthorized API request is rejected with HTTP 403.
  3. Work order completion and review sign-off are NOT blocked at the backend today: a direct API call from a role lacking the permission still succeeds (HTTP 200). This still passes v1 on the app-level restriction, but the backend gap is a known issue to fix later — note it as 'app blocks / backend allows'.
  4. Because several work-order permissions share the same backend check, any role with Work Orders: Create & Edit can receive parts onto a work order through the API.
  5. Unlike work order completion and review sign-off, the Bulk Receive 'accept' action IS enforced at the backend per role: the direct API call is rejected with HTTP 403 for the four roles that should not have it — Office, Sales Representative, Technician, Time Clock — and is allowed for the seven roles that should (Admin, Service Manager, Senior Service Advisor, Service Advisor, Foreman, Parts Manager, Parts Technician). This matches the permission matrix exactly, so Bulk Receive is genuinely backend-enforced.

title: Product Type multi-select: both toggles on by default; S/P prefix filtering
section_path: Reports Suite > Sales By Customer Report > SBC — Product Type Filter
refs: SV-8602 (SBC spec v20 2026-08-17 Story 3 S3-R1; S3-R2; S3-R3; S3-R4; S3-R5; S3-R6 — control redesigned from a single-select dropdown to a multi-select per SV-9074; S3-R2 CLOSES the list itself so the closed list IS the requirement)
preconds:
1. You are on the Sales By Customer report with no saved view (first visit or cleared browser storage), so the first-load default can be read.
2. The date range contains at least one service invoice (number starting with S) and one parts invoice (number starting with P) — seed ZZAUTOTEST data if needed.
steps:
1. Find the "Product Type" filter in the report toolbar; read its current selection before touching it, then open it and read the action rows and the toggle options in order.
2. Select only "Services" (leave "Parts" unselected), expand a customer down to invoice rows, and read the invoice numbers.
3. Select only "Parts" and read the invoice numbers again.
4. Use "All products" to select both toggles again.
expected:
1. The "Product Type" filter in the toolbar is a multi-select, behaving like the Customer and Location filters. Opened, it pins two action rows at the top — "All products" and "Clear all" — above two toggle options: "Parts" and "Services."
2. On first load both toggles are selected, so all products are included and no product-type filter is applied.
3. With only "Services" selected, every invoice shown has a number starting with S; parts invoices are gone and all counts/totals reflect only S invoices.
4. With only "Parts" selected, every invoice shown has a number starting with P; service invoices are gone and all counts/totals reflect only P invoices.
5. With both toggles selected again, no product-type filter is applied — both S and P invoices are included and counts/totals cover both.
6. The whole invoice is classified by its number prefix — there is no per-line-item split.
Note for the tester: the toggles read "Parts" and "Services", but the filter summary line printed in the exports uses the older wordings — "Parts & Service" with both toggles on, "Service only" with only Services on, and "Parts only" with only Parts on. That difference is expected and is not a fault.

---

title: Location column: shown to any multi-location user; toggleable; rep rows Multiple
section_path: Reports Suite > Sales By Representative Report > SBR — Location Filter
refs: SV-8638 (SBR spec v22 2026-08-17 S21-R7; S14-R20; renamed to Labor Delta per SV-9071)
preconds:
1. You are on the Sales By Representative report as a user with access to two or more locations.
  2. One rep has invoices at a single location and another rep has invoices at two different locations.
  3. Show Unassigned is turned on and at least one unassigned invoice exists.
steps:
1. Select two or more locations and read the column headers.
  2. Read the Location cell on the single-location rep's summary row.
  3. Read the Location cell on the rep whose invoices span two locations.
  4. Expand that rep and read an invoice detail row's Location cell.
  5. Read the Location cell on the Unassigned summary row.
  6. Check that the pinned Subtotal column is still the rightmost column.
  7. Narrow the selection to a single location and read the headers again.
  8. Open the column selector, switch Location off, read the headers again, then switch it back on.
  9. With more than one location still selected, download all four files from the ⋯ menu (Summary and Expanded View, PDF and CSV) and read the Location column in each one.
expected:
1. Because you have access to more than one location, a Location column is shown by default, positioned immediately after the Status column and before Labor Delta.
  2. A rep summary row whose invoices are all at one location shows that location's name.
  3. A rep summary row whose invoices span more than one location shows "Multiple".
  4. An invoice detail row shows that invoice's own exact location — never "Multiple".
  5. The Unassigned summary row follows the same rule as any rep summary row.
  6. The pinned Subtotal column is still rightmost — the Location column never displaces it.
  7. Narrowing the selection to a single location does NOT hide the column; it stays on screen.
  8. Switching Location off in the column selector removes it; switching it back on restores it in the same position.

  9. Whenever the column is shown on screen, all four downloads include it in the same position. In the Summary files a rep's row carries that rep's location and reads "Multiple" when the rep spans more than one location; in the Expanded View files each invoice row carries that invoice's own exact location.
    Note for the tester: whether this column appears depends on how many locations your login can reach, not on how many you have currently selected. Someone who can reach only one location never sees it at all. If it stays on screen after you narrow to a single location, that is correct.

Note for the tester about step 8: the column selector on this report lists the metric columns (Labor Delta, Labor Invoiced, Labor Margin, Parts Invoiced, Parts Margin, Adjustments, Margin, Margin %) and no Location entry, because the Location column is shown automatically rather than toggled. Step 8 therefore cannot be carried out as written: mark step 8 as blocked and record the other steps as normal.

preconds:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.

expected:

Even for someone who IS allowed to open it, the customer name is deliberately styled to look like ordinary text — same colour, no underline — so a name you can use and a name you cannot use look exactly the same. title: The Expanded View PDF's 10,000-row cap is enforced server-side BEFORE generation
section_path: Reports Suite > Sales By Representative Report > SBR — API
refs: SV-8631 (SBR spec v22 2026-08-17 Story 14 S14-E2)
preconds:
1. A filter set producing more than 10,000 invoice detail rows exists or can be seeded — otherwise mark Blocked-Env with the reason.
2. The network panel is open.
3. To see the information this test asks for you need the browser's own developer tools: press F12 (or Ctrl+Shift+I; on a Mac Cmd+Option+I) and open the "Network" tab, then reload the page. There is nothing to install — it is built into Chrome, Edge and Firefox..
steps:
1. Trigger "Download Expanded View (PDF)" against the over-cap filter set and observe the export request/response.
2. Check whether any file arrives.
expected:
1. The server counts the rows against the 10,000-data-row cap and DECLINES to generate — the refusal happens pre-generation, observed in the export response.
2. NO file (truncated or otherwise) is delivered; the client shows the specific too-large toast.
3. A filter set just below the cap still generates a complete (possibly very large) PDF.
What you should see today: the spreadsheet download works and produces a file, but the PDF download of the same view fails with a server error and no file arrives. It depends on how much is in the view, not on which report - filtered down to one or two rows the PDF downloads normally, and on a full unfiltered view of several thousand rows it fails every time. This is a known problem and it is already reported - see https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-8818
- If you see exactly that, mark this test FAILED and do not raise anything new.
- If it fails in a DIFFERENT way from what is described above, that is a NEW problem - please report it.
- If it PASSES, the fix has shipped: tell the QA lead so the ticket can be closed and this note removed.

title: Permission matrix: what each role sees versus what the server enforces
section_path: Founder Mode (September 2026) > Part Sales > Part Sales — QA Additions (Mudassir) > XC · Cross-cutting & handoff
preconds:
1. Six test users exist on the build under test and you can sign in as each: (1) Owner/Admin; (2) View-only — Part Sales View without Create & Edit, e.g. the Office User role; (3) No-access — a Technician who cannot open part sales; (4) Parts-only — Part Sales Create & Edit but NOT Invoicing & Payments Create & Edit; (5) Vendor-perm — Vendor and order management only (this build has no permission named "Vendors"); (6) No-portal — no Customer Portal access.
  2. A part sale CREATED on this build exists, not invoiced, holding a received part with a core.
steps:
1. As each user in turn, open the part sale (top menu Parts -> Part Sales -> click the sale; look at the parts list, the Financial Info card, the menu ( ... ) above the parts list and the Finance tab) and note whether these are OFFERED: Return Core, Cancel Return, Edit tax rate, Audit Log, Sales Representative, Add Deposit.
  2. As the View-only and Parts-only users, attempt each action by direct request (browser devtools re-send, or ask engineering to call the endpoint with that user's session).
  3. Record offered / hidden / server-refused per user per action.
expected:
Expected results

  • Admin: all six offered and allowed.
  • View-only: none offered; every direct request refused by the server.
  • No-access: cannot open the part sale at all (See Financial Data gate).
  • Parts-only: Return Core, Cancel Return, Edit tax rate, Audit Log, Sales Representative offered; Add Deposit NOT offered and refused by the server (needs Invoicing & Payments Create & Edit).
  • Vendor-perm: Return Core and Cancel Return offered (shared core control); the part-sale-only actions are not.
  • The server enforces the WORK-ORDER edit permission for tax, rep and deposit: a user holding either Part Sales Create & Edit or Work Orders Create & Edit is allowed through.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-9667 (Founder Mode Batch #1); Part Sales Update v1 PRD (Confluence 867434569), sections Permissions and enforcement, Form factor, Key Decisions; Review Decisions and Open Questions (Confluence 878673921); QA handoff comment on SV-9867 by Nemanja Djuric 30 Sep 2026; read 30 Sep 2026. title: For Customer on an attachment needs Edit, view-only users see it disabled
section_path: Founder Mode (September 2026) > Notifications > Specification update 2 October 2026 (QA Additions)
preconds:
1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user (the standard Admin role). This is User A.
  2. A work order at this location: top menu Work Orders -> Create Work Order, select a customer (e.g. "4 Star Truck Repair"), save.
  3. A part sale at this location: top menu Parts -> Part Sales -> New Part Sale, pick the Customer and click Save.
  4. The customer's own notes: top menu Customers -> open the customer (e.g. "4 Star Truck Repair") -> Notes tab.
  5. As User A, write a note with an attached photo on each of the work order, the part sale and the customer (New Note -> attach a file -> save).
  6. A teammate at the same location to tag, User B, who can sign in: on a QA branch the second user is the Tech quick-login user (sign in from a private browser window with the Tech button; appears as "Tech ShopView"). They are listed under Settings -> Staff. Create the test role: Settings (click your initials at the top right -> Settings) -> Roles & Permissions -> Create Custom Role -> in Choose a template pick "Service Advisor" -> Apply; tick Work orders -> Create & Edit, Part sales -> Create & Edit and Customers -> Create & Edit; enter the Role name "ZZAUTOTEST Editors" and click Create. Assign it: Settings -> Staff -> on User B's row click the edit icon -> in Edit Staff Member set Role to "ZZAUTOTEST Editors" -> Save & Close. User B must log out and back in before testing (a role change ends their session).
  7. A second teammate, User C. On a QA branch only two users can sign in (Admin and Tech): when a step says "Sign in as User C", first give Tech ShopView User C's role (Settings -> Staff -> on Tech ShopView's row click the edit icon -> Role -> Save & Close; Tech signs out and back in) and run that step as Tech ShopView. For tagging or group membership only, any staff member (e.g. "Ashlee Thomas") can be User C. Create the test role: Settings (click your initials at the top right -> Settings) -> Roles & Permissions -> Create Custom Role -> in Choose a template pick "Service Advisor" -> Apply; leave Work orders -> View, Part sales -> View and Customers -> View ticked, and untick their Edit permissions; enter the Role name "ZZAUTOTEST View only" and click Create. Assign it: Settings -> Staff -> on User C's row click the edit icon -> in Edit Staff Member set Role to "ZZAUTOTEST View only" -> Save & Close. User C must log out and back in before testing (a role change ends their session). Make sure the role's Work orders view is "Full View" (not "Tech View"): Tech View hides the For Customer checkbox on work order notes entirely (S10-R5b exception).
steps:
1. Sign in as User B (not the author). On each of the three notes, tick then clear For Customer on the photo.
  2. Sign in as User C and look at the For Customer checkbox on each photo.
expected:
Expected results

  • User B can tick and clear For Customer on all three, although they did not write the notes: it is not an edit to the note.
  • User C sees the For Customer checkbox disabled, still showing whether the customer sees the file.

Note (13 Oct 2026, SV-11247 – working as designed): S10-R5b exception — on work order and work order line notes, a role whose Work Orders view is set to Tech View (e.g. the default Technician role) does not see the For Customer checkbox at all, as today. The "disabled checkbox" expectation applies only to roles with Full View and no Edit (e.g. default Sales Representative on a WO note; Technician on a customer/asset note). User C's "ZZAUTOTEST View only" role must have Work Orders view = Full View for step 2 on the work order note. Chris confirmed 13 Oct; SV-10253 updated to match.

Source - where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-9667; story SV-10253 (S10, Who can do what); Notifications Update v1 PRD (Confluence 817463297) as edited 2 October 2026, S10; read 5 Oct 2026. Source-verified 5 October 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S10-R5b: “Ticking or clearing For Customer on an attachment is not an edit to the note. Any user with Edit for the kind of record it is on can do it: 'Work Orders → Edit' for a work order or work order line, 'Part Sales → Edit' for a part sale, and 'Customers → Edit' for a customer or an asset. A user who can only view the record sees the checkbox disabled, so they can still tell which files the customer sees.”

Last checked against build v26.40.7-7ffda69 on 10/5/2026.
